el Carmel — Barcelona, Spain

Average day Higher caution advised night

In detail

El Carmel has the strongest documented safety concerns in the district. Around the Bunkers del Carmel viewpoint, residents describe their street as 'the worst street in Barcelona,' citing a violent robbery by minors, an assault on a neighbour who confronted late-night revellers, vandalism, and squatters throwing large parties — prompting the city to install €1.4M anti-crowding fencing to close the viewpoint at 10pm. More recently: a mass brawl with a stabbing and 13 arrests at El Coll-La Teixonera metro station (5 Apr 2026), a suspect linked to ~16 break-ins arrested, and a kidnapping/attempted-murder arrest. Daytime risk is mainly pickpocketing/burglary; night-time, especially around the bunkers viewpoint and metro area, carries real risk of confrontational violence. Sources checked: Metròpoli Obert, 12 Nov 2022; elindependiente.com, 9 Apr 2023; barnadiario.com, Dec 2024-Apr 2026.
